note: Learning metadata only. Assessments do not authorize, deny, detect, or choose profile, grants, tools, or scopes. Splunk does not enforce.
instructor_prompt: Complete Same request, different defense without opening Path B.

blue_team_competencies.evidence_required: Completed hypothesis, SPL strategy, timeline, evidence ledger, revised conclusion, report, and threat-model bridge.

threat_modeling_competencies.evidence_required: Completed threat-model artifact with architecture summary, selected assets, actors, flows, boundaries, authority, prioritized threats, controls and placement, telemetry, gaps, residual risks, recommendations, and three audience-specific explanations.

privacy_data_governance_competencies.evidence_required: Completed data inventory, lifecycle and trace, minimization decision, privacy evidence ledger, privacy threat model, control strategy, residual-risk statement, and three audience-specific explanations.

dimensions.title: Trust boundary reasoning
dimensions.needs_review: Mixes data, claims, and grants. Cannot name where untrusted input meets a control.
dimensions.demonstrated: Names the boundary and what the attacker does not control.
dimensions.advanced: Separates multiple planes (input, context, identity, goal) without collapsing them into prompt injection.

dimensions.title: Authority reasoning
dimensions.needs_review: Treats OBSERVE as ALLOW, claims as authentication, or retrieved text as a grant.
dimensions.demonstrated: Names the actual PDP and says REQUEST != GRANT.
dimensions.advanced: Explains why a granted tool can still be the wrong goal, and why identity OBSERVE is not authn.

dimensions.title: Splunk investigation
dimensions.needs_review: Searches index=* or pastes Path B first.
dimensions.demonstrated: Uses quoted run.id, sequence, and event.name in Search.
dimensions.advanced: Chooses the right existing Q-* hunt without treating Studio tables as a fresh LIVE launch.

dimensions.title: Execution reconstruction
dimensions.needs_review: Reads ALLOW as execution or missing rows as prevention.
dimensions.demonstrated: Cites runtime handler/LLM count as authoritative where the lab defines it; Splunk as corroboration.
dimensions.advanced: States completeness limits (local vs dc(_raw); HEC 200 is not searchable evidence).

dimensions.title: ATTACK / RETEST comparison
dimensions.needs_review: Compares different payloads or calls RETEST universal security.
dimensions.demonstrated: Same adversarial bytes; different server-owned configuration; different decision/execution.
dimensions.advanced: Names what the experiment still cannot prove.

dimensions.title: Evidence quality
dimensions.needs_review: One field proves the whole outcome. Empty dashboard = SAFE.
dimensions.demonstrated: Classifies SUPPORTED / CORROBORATED / NOT PROVEN / INCORRECT.
dimensions.advanced: Rewrites false SOC sentences into defensible claims.

dimensions.title: Security communication
dimensions.needs_review: Says Splunk blocked, the agent authenticated, or RAG was trusted.
dimensions.advanced: Explains the same incident to a peer without repository jargon.

challenges.title: Who enforces, who observes?
challenges.security_question: Which component can ALLOW or DENY, and which component only copies telemetry?
challenges.task: In your own words: what is an agent, a tool, MCP in this lab, a trust boundary, and a PDP? Then answer who enforces versus who observes.
challenges.starter_context: Open Home ORIENT if the words are new. Do not launch anything yet.
challenges.hint_1: Studio is the syllabus. Attack Service is a closed launcher. AcmeBank is the runtime. Splunk Search is the notebook.
challenges.hint_2: A PDP is the control that authorizes or denies the dangerous operation. Some controls only OBSERVE. Splunk is never the PDP here.
challenges.expected_reasoning: AcmeBank coded controls enforce. Splunk indexes a copy. An agent is an LLM plus tools, memory, and a task. MCP here is the in-process tool interface. RAG and memory are data planes. run.id correlates one experiment.
supported_claims: Splunk does not ALLOW or DENY AgentSec requests.
not_proven_claims: That a learner who can define MCP could operate a production MCP mesh.
incorrect_claims: Splunk is the policy decision point.
Opening Home START means the control ALLOWED.
challenges.attacker_controlled: Nothing yet. This challenge has no launch.

challenges.title: Rewrite the indefensible sentence
challenges.security_question: Which of these claims are INCORRECT, and how would you rewrite them?
challenges.task: Rewrite each sentence so a SOC peer could defend it: (1) Splunk blocked the attack. (2) The RAG document was trusted. (3) The agent was authenticated. (4) No mcp.started means it did not execute. (5) MCP ALLOW means the goal was approved. (6) The RETEST proves prompt injection is solved.
challenges.starter_context: Use SUPPORTED / CORROBORATED / NOT PROVEN / INCORRECT. Home CHECK has similar claims.
challenges.hint_1: DATA != AUTHORITY. IDENTITY CLAIM != AUTHENTICATION. ALLOW != EXECUTION. MISSING EVENT != PREVENTION. RETEST SUCCESS != UNIVERSAL SECURITY.
challenges.hint_2: Provenance is not trust. OBSERVE is not ALLOW. HEC 200 is not searchable evidence.
challenges.expected_reasoning: Each original sentence is INCORRECT. Splunk observed. Provenance != trust. Caller id is a claim. Missing indexed start is corroborative only. Tool grant != authorized goal. One RETEST is one configuration.
incorrect_claims: No mcp.started proves non-execution by itself.
challenges.server_owned: Policy and grants (unchanged by this exercise).

challenges.title: Find this run without being told the mode
challenges.security_question: What evidence did this experiment generate, and what kind of experiment was it?
challenges.task: Do not assume BASELINE, ATTACK, or RETEST from the title. Open Search. Find this run.id. Reconstruct sequence. Read testbed.mode and profile from the events. Then say what the evidence is.
challenges.starter_context: index=agentsec_telemetry sourcetype=otel:agentic:json. Filter a quoted agentsec.run.id. Do not search index=*. This UUID is a canonical REPLAY specimen, not a launch you just minted.
challenges.hint_1: Sort by agentsec.sequence, not as if _time were authority. Read event.name.
challenges.hint_2: Look at agentsec.testbed.mode and agentsec.security.profile on the same events. Mode is a label. Profile is server-owned.
challenges.expected_reasoning: REPLAY specimen f39fed12-… is the labeled vulnerable ATTACK copy (testbed.mode=ATTACK, profile=vulnerable). Rows are an indexed copy. Index presence is not completeness.
supported_claims: This specimen is labeled ATTACK on the indexed events when those fields are present.
corroborated_claims: Event count on a complete copy matches the local pack for this historical run.
not_proven_claims: That you minted this UUID today.
That the model approved a loan.
incorrect_claims: This UUID is your fresh LIVE launch.
Finding rows means Splunk authorized the loan.
challenges.attacker_controlled: The loan input string (catalog ATK-002 bytes).
challenges.observability_only: Splunk copy of this historical run.

challenges.title: Decision versus execution
challenges.security_question: Which control decided, what did it decide, and did the protected operation execute?
challenges.task: On the same REPLAY run.id: identify the trust boundary, the control id, the decision and reason, whether llm.started exists, and what that does and does not mean. Name the PDP.
challenges.starter_context: Same index/sourcetype/quoted run.id. Filter event.name=agentsec.control.decision, then separately look at llm.started / llm.completed.
challenges.hint_1: Reuse Q-CONTROL-DECISION and Q-LLM-EXECUTED. Do not invent field names.
challenges.hint_2: ALLOW is not execution. On this vulnerable ATTACK copy, hop 0 is fail-open ALLOW and llm.* should appear on a complete copy. Runtime LLM invoke count is authoritative.
challenges.expected_reasoning: PDP is CTRL-INPUT-001 at AcmeBank HTTP before Ollama. Splunk copied ALLOW. Execution is llm.started / runtime invoke, not the ALLOW row. ATTACK success here is not universal prompt-injection vulnerability.
supported_claims: CTRL-INPUT-001 evaluated hop 0 on this specimen.
corroborated_claims: Indexed llm.started corroborates execution on a complete copy.
not_proven_claims: That the model approved the loan.

challenges.title: Same request, different defense
challenges.security_question: SAME what? DIFFERENT what? Why did the security outcome change?
challenges.task: Compare these two REPLAY run.ids in Search. Identify requested tool, CTRL-MCP-001 decision/reason, and whether execution began. State what remained identical and what changed. Do not call this universal MCP security.
challenges.starter_context: Two quoted run.ids. Index agentsec_telemetry sourcetype otel:agentic:json. Q-MCP-AUTHZ then Q-MCP-EXECUTED. These are canonical REPLAY specimens.
challenges.hint_1: Requested tool should be lookup_customer_tier on both. That tool is not in coded allowed_tools.
challenges.hint_2: ATTACK is labeled fail-open ALLOW then handler 1. RETEST is DENY tool_not_granted, handler 0. Same ungranted request. Different server-owned profile/ExperimentContext.
challenges.expected_reasoning: SAME: ungranted lookup_customer_tier request. DIFFERENT: profile/decision/execution. PDP is CTRL-MCP-001. Splunk did not DENY RETEST. Runtime handler count is authoritative for execution.
supported_claims: CTRL-MCP-001 is the tool PDP on both specimens.
corroborated_claims: Indexed mcp.started on ATTACK / absence on RETEST on complete copies.
challenges.attacker_controlled: The closed ungranted tool request bytes.

challenges.title: MCP ALLOW, but was the goal authorized?
challenges.security_question: CTRL-MCP-001 ALLOW on ATTACK and RETEST. Did that authorize the expanded goal?
challenges.task: Open Search on both REPLAY ids. Separate CTRL-GOAL-INTEGRITY-001 from CTRL-MCP-001. What was the authoritative task? What did the instruction propose? What executed? RETEST is not an MCP DENY lesson.
challenges.starter_context: Q-GOAL-INTEGRITY-AUTHORITY and Q-MCP-AUTHZ. Evidence mode REPLAY.
challenges.hint_1: Task summarize_lending_policy_options is server-owned. ATTACK/RETEST proposed extract_full_policy. lookup_policy stays granted.
challenges.hint_2: ATTACK: GOAL OBSERVE overlay, wrong-goal handler 1. RETEST: GOAL DENY unauthorized_task_expansion, wrong-goal handler 0, in-task handler 1. AUTHORIZED TOOL != AUTHORIZED GOAL.
challenges.expected_reasoning: MCP ALLOW answers tool grant. Goal control answers authorized purpose. RETEST still ALLOWs lookup_policy. Wrong-goal handler 0 is authoritative non-execution of the expansion.
supported_claims: CTRL-MCP-001 ALLOW lookup_policy on both specimens.
CTRL-GOAL-INTEGRITY-001 is not the tool PDP.
corroborated_claims: Indexed goal decision rows on a complete copy.
incorrect_claims: MCP DENY is the Goal lesson.
ALLOW means the expanded goal was approved.
challenges.server_owned: TaskContract, coded lookup_policy grant, goal control.

challenges.title: Identity OBSERVE is not authentication
challenges.security_question: CTRL-IDENTITY-001 emitted OBSERVE. Has the caller been authenticated?
challenges.task: Search both REPLAY ids. What did identity decide? What did CTRL-MCP-001 decide? Was anyone authenticated? Use NOT PROVEN / NOT MODELED where the lab does not model authentication.
challenges.hint_1: IDENTITY CLAIM != AUTHENTICATION. DELEGATION CLAIM != AUTHORIZATION. Caller agent id is data.
challenges.hint_2: CTRL-IDENTITY-001 stays OBSERVE identity_claim_is_not_grant on ATTACK and RETEST. The tool PDP is still CTRL-MCP-001 (ALLOW overlay vs DENY).
challenges.expected_reasoning: WHO AUTHENTICATED = NOT PROVEN / NOT MODELED. OBSERVE is classification. MCP is the grant decision. One RETEST is not universal identity security. This is not Confused Deputy (that is MCP-006 REPLAY).
incorrect_claims: Identity failure must explain every tool execution.
challenges.server_owned: coded grants, identity control OBSERVE semantics.
challenges.observability_only: Splunk. Identity control is OBSERVE, not a grant engine.

challenges.title: Empty mcp.started is not prevention
challenges.security_question: This RETEST copy has no mcp.started. Does that alone prove the handler never ran?
challenges.task: Search the REPLAY RETEST id. Find CTRL-MCP-001 DENY. Note missing mcp.started. Write what is authoritative versus corroborative. Mention completeness.
challenges.starter_context: Q-MCP-AUTHZ and Q-MCP-EXECUTED. Evidence mode REPLAY.
challenges.hint_1: MISSING EVENT != PREVENTION. Empty dashboard is insufficient. HEC 200 is insufficient.
challenges.hint_2: Runtime handler_invoke_count = 0 is authoritative non-execution where the lab defines it. Indexed absence corroborates only on a complete copy versus local events.jsonl.
challenges.expected_reasoning: No. Missing mcp.started is corroborative. DENY is authorization evidence. Handler 0 is authoritative. pytest does not prove live Splunk. 0 DET-MCP-001 rows is not SAFE.
supported_claims: CTRL-MCP-001 DENY tool_not_granted on this RETEST specimen.
corroborated_claims: No indexed mcp.started on a complete copy.
incorrect_claims: No mcp.started proves prevention by itself.
challenges.attacker_controlled: Same ungranted tool request as ATTACK.

challenges.title: Do not collapse every incident into prompt injection
challenges.security_question: How does SOURCE → BOUNDARY → INFLUENCE → AUTHORITY → EXECUTION → TELEMETRY → INVESTIGATION → CLAIM apply without treating every lab as the same attack?
challenges.task: For prompt/input, tool authorization, RAG, memory, goal integrity, identity, and the capstone: name the typical untrusted source, the control that classifies or decides, and whether that control is the tool PDP. Then say what would be a false conclusion if you mixed the labs.
challenges.starter_context: Home PATH + CONNECT blocks on each LIVE lab. No launch required.
challenges.hint_1: Only CTRL-MCP-001 grants tools. CTRL-INPUT-001 is the HTTP input PDP. RAG/memory/identity often OBSERVE. Goal is a different plane than MCP.
challenges.hint_2: Capstone retrieve→write→recall can be explained without Goal or Identity event families. 0 rows there != those domains never fail.
challenges.expected_reasoning: Same chain, different evidence. Input: CTRL-INPUT-001. Tools: CTRL-MCP-001. RAG/memory: data + MCP. Goal: task vs tool. Identity: claim vs grant. Capstone fuses RAG+memory+MCP. False: 'it executed so identity failed' or 'it is all prompt injection.'
supported_claims: CTRL-MCP-001 is the sole tool PDP in these labs.
not_proven_claims: That every production agent uses this exact control set.
incorrect_claims: Every AgentSec lab is prompt injection.
challenges.attacker_controlled: Varies by lab; never grants/tools/profile in the browser.

challenges.title: Lending assistant mastery readout
challenges.security_question: Can you produce an evidence-backed readout of retrieve → persist → later recall → tool authorization without Path B first?
challenges.task: Preferred: launch LIVE ATTACK and RETEST from Attack Service, copy retrieve/write/recall ids, investigate in Search. The listed ids below are official historical 16B copies: label them REPLAY, not a launch you just minted. Produce the 15-point readout on the RUBRIC tab. Path B Q-MCP-AUTHZ is a recall-run fragment, not that readout. Do not invent a retrieve-to-write field. Do not invent DET-CAPSTONE.
challenges.starter_context: index/sourcetype plus three quoted run.ids (retrieve, write, recall). Q-RUN-EVENTS, Q-RAG-CONTEXT-AUTHORITY, Q-MEMORY-CONTEXT-AUTHORITY, Q-MCP-AUTHZ, Q-MCP-EXECUTED. Completing Path B on one recall UUID is not the 15-point readout.
challenges.hint_1: Hash equality links retrieve content to what was stored. Recall source_run_id points at the write run. CTRL-MCP-001 is the tool PDP. RAG and memory OBSERVE.
challenges.hint_2: ATTACK recall: MCP ALLOW overlay, handler 1. RETEST recall: DENY tool_not_granted, handler 0. Goal/Identity 0 rows != those domains never fail. One RETEST != universal RAG/memory resistance.
challenges.expected_reasoning: See the 15-point capstone rubric. Attacker controls fixture bytes. Server owns grants/profile. PDP is CTRL-MCP-001. Splunk reconstructs a copy. Splunk cannot prove universal security or completeness without a local count.
supported_claims: CTRL-MCP-001 authorized or denied the follow-on tool.
corroborated_claims: Indexed mcp.started on ATTACK complete copy; handler 0 on RETEST is runtime.
not_proven_claims: Goal or identity caused this packet.
incorrect_claims: Missing Goal events mean Goal never fails.
Path B Q-MCP-AUTHZ on the official recall UUID is the 15-point readout.
The listed UUIDs are a fresh LIVE launch.
